messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Add a fused spur from an existing ring circuit in a living room", "project": "House in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "Sch 4 para 2", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(2) Work which— (a) is not in a kitchen, or a special location; (b) does not involve work on a special installation; and (c) consists of— (i) adding light fittings and switches to an existing circuit, or (ii) adding socket outlets and fused spurs to an existing ring or radial circuit."}, {"ref": "reg 12(6A)", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(6A) A person intending to carry out building work in relation to which Part P of Schedule 1 imposes a requirement is required to give a building notice or an application for building control approval with full plans where the work consists of— (a) the installation of a new circuit; (b) the replacement of a consumer unit; or (c) any addition or alteration to existing circuits in a special location."}, {"ref": "para 2.6", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.6 Diagram 2 illustrates the space around a bath tub or shower tray (a special location) within which minor additions and alterations to existing circuits, as well as the installation of new circuits, are notifiable. See paragraphs 2.5 to 2.6 600mm 600mm 2.25m Bath tub or shower tray Additions and alterations to existing circuits are notifiable in the shaded area Diagram 2 NOTE: Socket-outlets should not be located within 3m of a bath tub or shower tray Notifiable work in rooms containing a bath or shower Non-notifiable work"}]}

message.content:
Adding a fused spur to an existing ring circuit in a living room is **not notifiable**.

- **Schedule 4 paragraph 2(c)(ii)** covers "adding socket outlets and fused spurs to an existing ring or radial circuit". Work listed in Schedule 4 does not need a notice.
- **The exclusions do not apply.** A living room is not a kitchen or a special location (the space around a bath or shower, per Approved Document P paragraph 2.6), and the work does not involve a special installation.
- **Regulation 12(6A) is not triggered.** The work is not a new circuit, not a consumer unit replacement, and not work in a special location.

The work must still meet Part P, even though no notice is needed.
